PullRequest.Title: new session chat input revamp
PullRequest.Body: Supersedes #338076 with a production-hardened version of the same Calm progressive-disclosure direction. This intentionally does not close the original PR while review moves to the replacement. ## What changed - keeps the new composer layout fully behind `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` (with the unified workspace picker), restoring the legacy placement when disabled - groups the workspace, repository (worktree/branch), and harness controls into a collapsible session-options tray above the prompt, styled as a tab that is left-aligned and joined to the input with a shoulder - when collapsed, keeps the repository and harness pickers as an always-available icon rail rather than hiding them, controlled by `sessions.chat.experimental.collapsedSessionOptionsShowIcons` (default on, ExP-controllable with a triggered scorecard) - remembers the expanded/collapsed disclosure state across composers - never collapses the options while a screen reader is active, dropping the disclosure toggle so the pickers stay in the accessibility tree - shows all picker labels when there is room, then compacts them one at a time from right to left as the composer narrows, keeping the workspace name visible; measures against the whole prompt toolbar so the pickers no longer over-compact to icons with room to spare - demotes the getting-started tip to a rounded notice below the input so it no longer sits between the pickers and the field - replaces the draft-session worktree checkbox with a New Worktree / Branch dropdown, preserving provider-defined options, configuration resolution, and Dev Container restrictions, and announcing the disabled reason to screen readers - stops the workspace picker flickering shut on a touch tap by ignoring the ghost click that follows a Gesture Tap - fixes screen-reader descriptions, conditional accessibility help, heading typography, corner radii, responsive layout, and high-contrast/focus behavior ## Follow-up updates (2026-09-29) - restored the in-session experimental composer behavior to match #337149 (no additional redesign changes) - moved running-session Agent Mode + Approvals pickers into the main chat-input toolbar under the experimental layout gate, with legacy fallback to secondary toolbar when the experiment is off - aligned context usage placement/trailing space with the send-button-side composition used in #337149 - preserved split-session width safety behavior from #337490 (`∞` width in split, centered cap in single-pane) ## Product rationale Progressive disclosure keeps the common case calm without hiding capability. The collapsed icon rail keeps every control reachable in one glance, so the tray reads as a simplification rather than removed functionality, while the disclosure expands to full labels on demand. Because the icons-vs-hidden choice only affects a collapsed tray, its experiment logs a trigger at the moment the composer collapses so the scorecard is not diluted by users who never collapse. ## Validation - `npm run transpile-client` ✅ passed (latest follow-up changes) - `npm run typecheck-client` (earlier iteration) - targeted ESLint and Stylelint (earlier iteration) - focused unit tests across the new chat widget, workspace picker, Harness picker, accessibility help, and Agent Host config picker (earlier iteration) - component fixtures for default, experimental, collapsed, icon-rail, expanded, narrow, light, dark, and high-contrast states, plus screenshot-stability checks (earlier iteration) - verified live in a Code OSS Agents window in both the default and experimental composers (earlier iteration) Draft for continued UI iteration.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous callback, clone/attach/geometry-read implementation, resize reachability, and per-item retry loop are directly traced. Only the exact frame-time impact varies with DOM size and hardware, which is reflected in medium severity rather than lower confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Deep-cloned DOM nodes plus synchronous style/layout geometry reads
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with every ResizeObserver delivery while the composer is resized, multiplied by the number of compactable picker items because each failed fit trial calls _fitsAvailableWidth again; each trial clones and measures the full tray subtree.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased main-thread layout/GC pressure and dropped frames while dragging or resizing the Sessions pane
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The workspace/repository/harness row had no ChatInputPickerResponsiveLayout, so resizing it did not repeatedly clone and synchronously measure this subtree.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new responsive layout observes the full workspace-picker container, and usePreferredWidth routes every fit check directly through _measurePreferredLayout. That helper deep-clones the observed subtree, attaches it, and reads every item and lane rect; the compaction loop can repeat this once per picker during each synchronous resize callback.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1312 newly enables usePreferredWidth for a newly-created responsive layout over the session-options container; before this hunk there was no responsive observer or intrinsic clone-and-measure loop for that row.
Findings.Title: Avoid cloning the options tray for every resize trial
Findings.Impact: With the experimental composer enabled, continuously resizing a split Sessions pane runs several attach/measure/remove cycles per delivered width (workspace plus repository/harness controls), blocking the browser's resize/layout phase and causing visible resize jank.
Findings.Evidence: ChatInputPickerResponsiveLayout constructs an unthrottled DisposableResizeObserver whose callback calls layout synchronously. layout tests each visible item until the lane fits; with usePreferredWidth, _fitsAvailableWidth always calls _measurePreferredLayout, which cloneNode(true)s the lane, appends it, and forces getBoundingClientRect reads. The changed fixture explicitly exercises widths 520/420/360/300/220, establishing that realistic pane widths require multiple right-to-left compaction trials.
Findings.Recommendation: Coalesce resize handling to one animation-frame pass and avoid rebuilding the measurement subtree for each candidate. Cache/invalidate intrinsic item widths when picker content changes, or build one measurement host per layout pass and derive the successive compact states from those measurements while preserving right-to-left compaction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or drag a split Sessions pane while the experimental new-session composer and session-options tray are visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ResizeObserver invokes ChatInputPickerResponsiveLayout.layout synchronously in the browser resize-observation phase; each intrinsic fit trial clones, attaches, and measures the tray before the next frame can paint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deep-clone the picker lane, attach the clone, and force DOM geometry reads for the lane and each item
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one clone/measurement per delivered width and up to one per visible picker compact trial when the lane remains too wide
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The session-options row had no responsive-layout observer or clone-and-measure loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous before resize/layout can complete and the frame can paint

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of delivered pane widths times the effective visible picker count (workspace plus repository/isolation/branch/harness controls); narrow widths require successive right-to-left compact trials.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All work is serialized on the UI thread. ResizeObserver delivery is unthrottled and there is no animation-frame coalescing or reuse across fit trials.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no width or measurement cache. Cold and warm resize passes both create a fresh deep clone for each preferred-width check; mutations only disconnect the observer during the current pass.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: callback scheduling, loop structure, deep cloning, DOM attachment, and forced geometry reads are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame loss depends on hardware, theme DOM complexity, and drag cadence; the synchronous mechanism and repeated cardinality are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity layout regression; submitted as a synchronous-ui-work finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create, expand, or collapse the experimental new-session composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction restores the tray preference and immediately persists the observed value; toggling changes hidden/inert/classes and synchronously reruns responsive layout before interaction returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and store the profile-scoped expanded boolean
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read and one immediate write per composer construction, then one write per expanded-state change
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No session-options preference was read or persisted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs during widget construction or directly in the toggle autorun; the payload is a single boolean and storage is expected to buffer persistence

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update tray DOM state and rerun responsive layout
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No disclosure transition or tray-specific responsive pass existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous interaction work; bounded except for the separately reported repeated intrinsic measurement mechanism

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One restore plus one immediate store per NewChatWidget lifetime, then one store and one layout pass per user toggle or relevant configuration/accessibility change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single main-thread autoruns; storage calls and DOM updates are serialized. No queue or burst is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The preference is read from profile storage, but the restored value is written back immediately even when unchanged. The operation is bounded to one boolean and does not grow with history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call count and reachability; low concern because payload and event frequency are bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The backing storage flush implementation is abstracted, but the value and call count are tightly bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the resize measurement issue; persistence and toggle work are bounded and infrequent.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or change Agent Host isolation/branch configuration in a draft session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the new isolation dropdown builds two local static items and does not call the provider completion boundary. Selecting a value reaches provider.setSessionConfigValue and configuration resolution; branch opening may await branch completions before the picker appears.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve session configuration after selecting isolation or branch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider update/resolve per accepted user selection, serialized per session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior isolation checkbox invoked the same provider update once per changed selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Selection completion/config refresh awaits the provider operation; the dropdown conversion does not increase call count

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load branch completion items from the Agent Host connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold request per draft session, shared by _branchLoad; zero additional requests on warm opens
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The branch picker already loaded the same coalesced completion list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold branch picker opening waits for the completion list; isolation picker opening does not reach this boundary

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Isolation is fixed at two items. Branch UI scales with returned branch count, but the changed isolation path does not fan out per branch and branch behavior is pre-existing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Repository config mutations are sequenced per session by repositoryConfigSequencer. Branch loading uses a shared promise per draft session, so concurrent/repeated opens coalesce after the first request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Isolation has no remote lookup. Branch load is cold once through _branchLoad and warm opens reuse the resolved/in-flight promise; dynamic labels are evicted to the current session and remain bounded by current properties/items.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the isolation early return, provider call path, per-session sequencer, and branch promise cache are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote duration and branch count vary by repository, but neither boundary frequency nor concurrency is increased by this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the new isolation dropdown preserves one provider mutation per selection and adds no completion request.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle the experimental running-session composer layout or cross the phone-layout breakpoint
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration/context events reparent existing mode/permission/context-usage DOM and invoke toolbar/editor relayout synchronously; no provider operation is awaited.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed number of toolbar controls and one context-usage widget; independent of message history and session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized event handlers on the UI thread; one update per configuration or breakpoint event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; unchanged values are guarded for editor trailing space, while reparenting occurs only on relevant setting/context changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High after tracing ChatView and NewChatInput autoruns and menu registrations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Toolbar DOM size varies slightly by provider, but event frequency and item count are small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; synchronous work is bounded to infrequent setting/breakpoint transitions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate the workspace picker by touch
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Gesture Tap opens the picker; the following browser ghost click is stopped and returns before a second show/toggle operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and populate the existing workspace picker
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per touch activation after the diff versus Tap plus ghost Click invocation before it
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both Tap and the browser-generated Click called showPicker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first open remains on the interaction path; the duplicate toggle is removed

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One tap and at most one guarded click per touch activation; workspace collection size remains handled by the existing picker.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event handlers run serially. The 500 ms guard removes the duplicate activation rather than creating concurrent loads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing workspace/provider caches are unchanged; the diff only suppresses a duplicate activation event.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the separate Tap/Click handlers and deterministic test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific workspace loading cost varies, but the diff strictly reduces activation cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 31 changed files and all diff pages. One concrete regression was reported: the new session-options responsive layout performs repeated deep DOM cloning and forced measurement synchronously during pane resize. Agent Host picker boundaries, storage lifecycle, running-session reparenting, touch activation, caches, concurrency, and disposal paths were traced and did not introduce additional reportable regressions.
